# Interaction & UX Checklist: Issues — creation, detail and editing

**Purpose**: Validate that the interaction, editing, validation, rendering and accessibility requirements in `spec.md` are complete, unambiguous and objectively verifiable, before the feature is decomposed into tasks
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [contracts/screens.md](../contracts/screens.md) · [contracts/markdown.md](../contracts/markdown.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Provenance of the marks below**: every item was evaluated and marked by Claude on 2026-08-31, at the reviewer's explicit instruction to review the checklist, mark what was already true with citations, and apply the recommended fix to the rest. Each item carries its verdict: **Yes** means the requirement already satisfied the criterion and names where; **Fixed** means the specification was changed to satisfy it and names the change. A reviewer who disagrees with a verdict should uncheck that item — the citations are there to be argued with.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

This is a **requirements-quality** review, not a verification pass. Every item asks whether something is *written well*, not whether code *works*.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are loading-state requirements defined for either screen, given that both are served by queries and R2 fixes a skeleton convention this feature never invokes? [Gap] — **Fixed**: `FR-067` requires a per-screen skeleton on both, below each route's authorization decision, applying the convention R2 fixes; `SC-021` makes it measurable.
- [x] CHK002 Are requirements defined for how an issue with no description renders, distinct from one whose description is empty markdown? [Gap, Spec §FR-044] — **Fixed**: `FR-044` now requires nothing rendered where the description would be, and the absent and empty cases treated identically — a user cannot tell them apart either.
- [x] CHK003 Is the save keystroke specified for keyboards without a Command key, or is ⌘-enter stated as the only accelerator deliberately? [Gap, Spec §FR-048] — **Fixed**: `FR-048` now requires the platform's own command modifier with Enter, so a keyboard without a Command key uses Control.
- [x] CHK004 Are requirements defined for submitting the create form without ever blurring the required field, given that validation is specified as per-field and on blur? [Gap, Spec §FR-037] — **Fixed**: `FR-037` now requires validation to run again on submit for every field, so a form submitted with nothing blurred reports on the fields rather than accepting the write.
- [x] CHK005 Are focus-management requirements defined for what receives focus after an in-place edit saves, reverts, or is refused? [Gap, Spec §FR-048, §FR-050] — **Fixed**: `FR-048` now requires focus in the field when edit mode opens and returned to the value on save, revert or refusal — never lost to the document.
- [x] CHK006 Is it specified what value the copy-link control places on the clipboard — the full address, the key, or something else? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-042] — **Fixed**: `FR-042` now requires the issue's full address, the one the browser shows, so what is pasted opens the issue for whoever receives it.
- [x] CHK007 Are requirements defined for whether a successful write produces any confirmation at all, given that §4 defines a success toast kind and no requirement here calls for one? [Gap, Spec §FR-050] — **Fixed**: `FR-050` now states it deliberately: no success toast, because the settled value is the confirmation and a toast per field edit would make the common case the noisy one.
- [x] CHK008 Are the concrete markdown tokens specified anywhere in the requirements, given that roadmap §1.1 assigned the subset's design to this child spec and the spec names constructs without naming their syntax? [Gap, Spec §FR-009, Roadmap §1.1] — **Fixed**: `FR-009` now carries the concrete syntax — every construct's spelling, `_` carrying no meaning, no escapes, no autolinks, no nesting. The design has moved from the plan into the requirement, where the roadmap assigned it.
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for pasting multi-line content into the single-line title field? [Gap, Spec §FR-049] — **Fixed**: `FR-049` now requires pasted line breaks collapsed to spaces and the paste accepted, since a refusal would discard what the user pasted.

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK010 Is "a message naming what failed and why" reconciled with §4's toast convention — is the channel specified, or may an implementer choose inline text? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-050, §4] — **Fixed**: `FR-050` now names the channel — a toast of the error kind, per §4 — and requires the rolled-back value visible as well.
- [x] CHK011 Is "grows with its content" quantified with a bound, or is unbounded growth intended? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-031, §FR-049] — **Fixed**: `FR-049` now bounds it: grows to the height at which the page scrolls, then scrolls within itself.
- [x] CHK012 Can "the page MUST render identically for every user in structure" be objectively evaluated, and is "structure" defined? [Measurability, Spec §FR-047] — **Fixed**: `FR-047` now defines identical in structure: same elements, same order, none absent for one user, and none changing between a control and plain text.
- [x] CHK013 Is "the key MUST be the page's first element" stated in terms a reviewer can apply — first in reading order, in the DOM, or in the visual layout? [Clarity, Spec §FR-042] — **Fixed**: `FR-042` now says first in reading order — first in the document, and therefore first for a screen reader and the keyboard as well as visually.
- [x] CHK014 Is the confirmation's required sentence specified precisely enough that two implementers would produce the same wording, or only its required content? [Clarity, Spec §FR-062] — **Yes**: `FR-062` fixes the required *content* — key, title, the size of the cascade, and the zero case — which is a specification's proper level. Exact wording is not a requirement, and pinning it would be.
- [x] CHK015 Is "in-flight state" defined for the Create control beyond the control not being idle? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038] — **Yes**: §4's *Slow write* row defines it — the control shows in-flight state and is interactive-blocked only for itself — and `FR-038`, `FR-015` and US1 scenario 6 fix what it must and must not display.

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK016 Are the two write surfaces' validation requirements consistent — does the create form and the issue page refuse an over-length value in the same terms? [Consistency, Spec §FR-037, §FR-049] — **Yes**: `FR-037` and `FR-049` state the same treatment, and `FR-049` says so explicitly: the two write surfaces refuse an over-length value the same way.
- [x] CHK017 Are the description requirements consistent between the create form and the issue page, including the absence of a preview and a toolbar on both? [Consistency, Spec §FR-031, §FR-044] — **Yes**: `FR-031` binds the create form to `FR-009`'s subset and `FR-044` forbids a preview or toolbar on both surfaces by name.
- [x] CHK018 Do the optimistic-write requirements agree about which writes are optimistic and which wait, with creation and in-place editing on opposite sides consistently? [Consistency, Spec §FR-038, §FR-050, §FR-051] — **Yes**: `FR-015` and `FR-038` put creation on the waiting side; `FR-050` and `FR-051` put in-place edits and the rail on the optimistic side. No requirement crosses.
- [x] CHK019 Are the disabled-state requirements for the title and description consistent with those for the rail's controls, in wording as well as in effect? [Consistency, Spec §FR-051, §FR-054] — **Yes**: `FR-054` requires the same disabled reason as the rail, in those words.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK020 Is "in under one minute and with no step outside the create form" accompanied by a stated measurement method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001] — **Fixed**: `SC-001` now states the basis: from the create form rendering to the issue page rendering, for a member who has done it before, bounding steps rather than server speed.
- [x] CHK021 Is "visible within one interaction" defined well enough to distinguish a conforming implementation from one that waits for the server? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006] — **Fixed**: `SC-006` now says *before the server has answered* — not merely quickly, but without waiting on the response at all.
- [x] CHK022 Does the markdown criterion enumerate the constructs it counts, so that "exactly the seven supported constructs" is checkable against a list? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-013] — **Yes**: `SC-013` counts seven and `FR-009` is the enumeration, now with each construct's syntax alongside.
- [x] CHK023 Is there a measurable criterion covering the rail's four controls as a set, or only criteria covering individual behaviours? [Coverage, Spec §SC-006, §SC-012] — **Yes**: `SC-006` covers all six editable fields as a set — the four rail controls plus title and description — and `SC-012` covers every control on the screen.

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK024 Are accessibility requirements defined for associating each disabled control's inline reason with the control programmatically, rather than only placing it nearby? [Gap, Spec §FR-026] — **Fixed**: `FR-068` now requires each reason associated with its control programmatically, so it reaches assistive technology as that control's explanation; `SC-022` makes it measurable.
- [x] CHK025 Are keyboard requirements defined for the in-place editing gesture — how a keyboard-only user enters edit mode on a value that is described as clicked? [Gap, Spec §FR-048] — **Fixed**: `FR-048` now requires the value focusable and edit mode reachable from the keyboard without a pointer.
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements stated that no state on these screens is conveyed by colour alone, given that column and priority both carry colour? [Gap, Spec §FR-051] — **Fixed**: `FR-068` requires a text or shape equivalent for a column's colour, a priority's colour and every validation state.
- [x] CHK027 Are any performance or responsiveness targets stated for either screen, or is their absence deliberate? [Gap] — **Fixed**: *Out of Scope* now records the absence deliberately, and names what is fixed instead: behavioural requirements (`SC-006`, `FR-038`) rather than timing ones.
- [x] CHK028 Are requirements defined for the confirmation dialog's focus behaviour — trap, initial focus and dismissal — rather than only that it confirms once? [Gap, Spec §FR-061] — **Fixed**: `FR-061` now requires the dialog to take focus, hold it, dismiss on Escape and on an explicit cancel, return focus to the Delete control, and never open with the destructive action focused.

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for a description whose markdown is malformed — an unclosed emphasis run, an unterminated link — rather than only for unsupported constructs? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-009] — **Fixed**: `FR-009` now requires anything the grammar does not match — an unclosed run, an unterminated link — to render as the characters typed, never as an error, with a matching edge case.
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for what the rail shows when the assignee pool is empty, or the project has exactly one column? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-022, §FR-052] — **Fixed**: Two new edge cases: an empty pool offers a control that can only be left unassigned, not an absent one; a single-column project offers one option, already the issue's own.
- [x] CHK031 Are the edge cases the spec lists for editing traced to a functional requirement each, or do some appear only as edge-case bullets? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases] — **Fixed**: All 26 edge cases now trace to a requirement. The three that did not — concurrent edits, a past due date, and the length boundary — are now `FR-064`, `FR-006` and `FR-008`.

## Notes

- Every item is marked; see **Provenance of the marks** above for who marked them and what each verdict means
- Uncheck any item whose verdict you disagree with — each carries the citation it rests on
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK008 was the largest finding and is now closed the way the roadmap intended: `FR-009` carries the concrete syntax — every construct's spelling, `_` carrying no meaning, no escapes, no autolinks, no nesting — and [contracts/markdown.md](../contracts/markdown.md) now restates that grammar rather than originating it, with `FR-009` winning where the two differ
- Twenty-three of the thirty-one were resolved by changing the specification. Accessibility and loading were the two blind spots: neither had a single requirement before this pass, and both now do (`FR-067`, `FR-068`, `SC-021`, `SC-022`)
